newsitem.title: CHINA: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.
newsitem.headline: China interbank market rates (CHIBOR) mostly up.

text.p: Following is the China Interbank Offered Rate (CHIBOR) for Monday issued by the official Xinhua news agency on behalf of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
The figures represent weighted averages and not closing prices and are annual percentage rates.
The central bank does not post volumes.
Traders said the rates went up today because of a forthcoming issue of China's first seven-year treasury bond.
A public tender for the rights to underwrite the issue will be held late this month and banks and institutions are borrowing money to prepare for the underwriting, traders said.
"Banks and other financial institutions borrowed money on the market today, leading to a temporary shortage of money supply and pushing up the rates," said one trader.
